Read the usable range from Results under the stated gain/current limits. Compare each range against the low- and high-rail sensor conditions.
The saved fixtures give 2.66 and 2.62 µA at 0.70 V. Their usable ranges are 0.62–1.80 V for NMOS and 0–0.78 V for PMOS, favoring opposite rails.
interview-gain/gain: Use measured gm and output conductance to explain the effect of bias and a 50 kΩ load.
Run the VG = .64, .65 and .66 V drain sweeps. Open Results and read the magnitude of I(VD).
Compare computed gm, ro and gain at VDS = 0.08 and 0.80 V. Replace ro with ro ∥ 50 kΩ for the loaded estimate.
Use gm ≈ ΔID/ΔVG, ro ≈ ΔVD/ΔID, and Av ≈ −gm(ro ∥ 50 kΩ). Near the low drain voltage, larger gds lowers gain.
interview-slew/slew: Distinguish small-signal response, large-signal slew and final tracking error across both loads.
Run the small-step and four large-step cases. In Results select out and compare rising and falling edges from 2 µs.
Read 10–90% time, 2% dynamic settling and DC command error separately. Calculate a slope from the nearly linear portion.
The example 500 mV fall takes about 141 ns at 2 pF and 384 ns at 8 pF. A larger load needs more charge. Settling accuracy and final error remain separate measurements.
interview-noise/noise: Compare integrated input and output noise and identify the largest source terms.
Run the 1 kΩ and 100 kΩ noise fixtures. Open Results and compare the same 10 Hz–1 MHz band.
Read input-referred RMS, output RMS and the largest named contributors. Inspect the spectrum and resistor value together.
The ideal source resistor has about 4.1 versus 40.7 nV/√Hz at room temperature. Compare the captured integrated noise and contributors separately. Square and sum independent terms.
interview-mismatch/mismatch: Quantify the effect of device area on offset spread and of unequal loads on offset mean.
Run the 64 seeded trials per area and open both histograms. Read mean, sigma and count within ±8 mV.
Compare whose distribution narrows. As a separate trial, match RL to RR in both cells and rerun the same seed.
Quadrupling area roughly halves input-referred sigma. Changing RL from 15.3 kΩ to match RR at 15 kΩ targets the systematic mean rather than the random width.
interview-comparator/comparator: Compare regeneration delay and input kickback at two overdrive levels.
Run the 3 mV and 40 mV cases at 0.90 V common mode and open Results.
From the 20 ns clock edge, measure the output crossing for OUTN−OUTP = 0.9 V. Separately plot either input against its source to inspect kickback.
The 3 mV case starts closer to metastability and decides more slowly. Input kickback is read on INP/INN relative to the source, not from the output edge.
interview-sar/sar-fault: Measure the MSB error and distinguish it from acquisition error and hold pedestal.
Keep the faulty C3 unchanged and run both driver cases. Plot hold around 50 ns and around the 75 ns MSB event.
Read settled acquisition error, pedestal and MSB step. Compare fast and slow cases before inferring the code.
With C3 = 650 fF the MSB step is too small. Compare it to the 0.80 V target. Diagnose using the fast driver so slow acquisition is not mistaken for bad bit weight.
interview-sar/sar-repair: Restore the MSB step to within 25 mV of 0.80 V while preserving the other capacitor values.
Choose Open circuit and locate C3. Set it to the sum of the three smaller binary capacitors plus the dummy unit.
Run the same two acquisition cases. In Results check MSB step and fast-driver acquisition, then compare the code at 0.76 V.
Set C3 to 800 fF. The corrected MSB step is approximately 0.80 V and the fast-driver acquisition error is within 15 mV.
interview-ldo/ldo: Measure DC dropout, load/ESR response, rail-step rejection and startup under the saved LDO fixtures.
Run all saved LDO testbenches. Compare the two 25–100 µA load-step cases at 120 pF in Results.
Find the last exit from the 2% band around 1.20 V, compare damping at both ESRs, then inspect the gate and output in the VIN sweep.
Read dropout from the DC input sweep when gate drive saturates. Compare ESR using the same load step, the line-step at fixed load, and startup from the supply ramp as separate evidence.
interview-post-layout-debug/route-baseli: Capture a schematic pass and an extracted timing miss on the supplied interconnect.
Open workspace in Layout and leave vout at 0.20 µm. Choose Compare interconnect.
Open Results and compare the schematic and extracted 2% settling times against 50 ps.
The schematic settles within 50 ps and the extracted 0.20 µm case exceeds 50 ps under the same stimulus.
interview-post-layout-debug/route-repair: Restore extracted precision settling to 50 ps or less while preserving connectivity.
Select the vout path in Layout and increase its width while keeping the endpoints.
Re-run the same interconnect comparison. Check both settling times and geometry before picking the final width.
Set the route width to 0.40 µm. The schematic waveform stays the same and measured extracted settling drops below 50 ps.
l-fold/single: Verify the original single-finger GF180 NMOS through process DRC and LVS.
Choose Open workspace and locate the gate, source, drain and body access in single_finger.
Set up Magic and Netgen if prompted. Run process DRC/LVS and open Results for the original layout.
Use the supplied one-finger, 2 µm total-width device with its linked body tie and ports. Require actual process DRC and matching extraction.
l-fold/folded: Generate and verify four fingers at the same total width and channel length.
Choose Open workspace, switch to Schematic and select MN1. Note its starting finger count, W and L.
Choose Generate device layout to set four fingers at the same W and L. In Layout inspect the alternating diffusions, then choose Run process DRC/LVS.
Set nf = 4, W = 2 µm total and L = 0.28 µm. Each finger is 0.50 µm wide. Read both process results.
l-body/tie: Connect the floating body to SOURCE without joining gate or drain.
Open Layout. Find the left body contact and source landing on metal1.
Draw a metal-1 path between them on SOURCE. Run process DRC/LVS and confirm the removed open.
Connect (−2.50, 1.00) to (−0.50, 1.00) µm with a 0.40 µm metal1 path labelled SOURCE.
l-match/balance: Match the active placement centroid and bring the two input route resistances within 5%.
Open workspace. Keep the two end dummies and compare the positions of the middle four devices.
Move the inner units to equalize centroids. Inspect the routes at Y = +4 and −4 µm, then adjust the narrower path.
Use dummy–A–B–B–A–dummy. Widen inp to 0.40 µm to match inn. The model gives 60 Ω on each input.
l-dac/array: Place seven identical tiles in the three bit groups so the intended capacitance ratio is 1:2:4.
Open workspace and show the unit_capacitor layer. Count the tiles on each rail.
Select the outlying upper tile and move it onto the upper row alongside the existing three. Preserve size and y coordinate.
Move C23 so its center is X = 8.5 µm. The rows then have 1, 2 and 4 ten-femtofarad units.
l-dac/baseline: Measure the original routed DAC code levels and isolate the disturbed bit weight.
Open workspace and identify the three bit rails and the common top plate.
Trace the long bit2 stub close to the top plate. Use Check this step and record the effective weights and endpoint-normalized INL.
Leave bit2_stub in place for the baseline. The nearby top plate increases the effective MSB weight and the baseline peak INL exceeds 0.23 LSB.
l-dac/repair: Reduce peak endpoint INL below 0.16 LSB without disconnecting any capacitor units.
Select the extra bit2 stub, identify where the four active tiles join the main rail, and remove only the unused branch.
Check connectivity and read the new bit weights and eight code levels.
Delete bit2_stub with the seven unit tiles and top plate intact. Effective weights return to 10, 20 and 40 fF.
l-lvs/open: Repair the open so inp reaches the correct far terminal.
Choose Open workspace on the open case and use Check this step to read the failure.
Trace the upper input conductor and bridge the gap to its far pad on metal1. Check the same case again.
Extend the inp route along Y = 4 µm to X = 12 µm, or bridge that open with a legal metal1 path. Keep inn separate.
l-lvs/short: Isolate inp from inn while preserving both intended routes.
Open workspace on the short case. Zoom to the two horizontal routes and identify their joining segment.
Remove the unintended bridge, leaving both routes and pads. Check connectivity again.
Delete the vertical metal1 bridge at X = 6 µm. Both horizontal routes remain continuous individually.
l-lvs/swap: Correct the swapped extraction port names without moving the physical input routes.
Open workspace on the swapped case and read the mismatched pin from Check this step.
Choose Edit input ports and assign the physical upper and lower terminals to the intended signals.
Assign inp to the upper terminal at Y = +4 µm and inn to the lower at Y = −4 µm.
l-eco/update: Increase the shared transistor width to 3 µm and update its linked layout safely.
Open shared_device in Schematic. Set MN1 total width to 3 µm.
Choose Review layout update. Inspect the new device dimensions and attached routes, then apply.
Use W = 3u in the schematic and the accepted linked-device update. The child ports and attached routes stay connected.
l-eco/parent: Verify both parent placements adopt the update while retaining their connections.
Open shared_parent and select X1 and X2. Read the referenced master in each inspector.
Trace clk through both GATE ports. Review the child and parent connectivity.
Both X1 and X2 reference shared_device and both GATE ports remain on clk. The updated master is shared.
l-settle/baseline: Record the original schematic and extracted differential errors at the 1.4 ns sample point.
Open workspace and leave both outp/outn stubs. Choose Run RC comparison.
Open Results. Compare the 1.4 ns differential output with the settled 2.5 ns schematic reference.
The original extracted differential error exceeds 12 mV. The stubs load the outputs even though they carry little DC current.
l-settle/repair: Reduce extracted differential error to at most 12 mV while keeping balanced output routing.
Open Layout and select only the two wide open-ended branches from outp and outn.
Delete both stubs, leaving the horizontal routes and pads. Run the same comparison and read the error.
Remove the two open-ended output stubs symmetrically. The teaching run gives extracted error below 2 mV.
l-noise/close: Capture victim disturbance for the original close same-layer clock route.
Open noise_close and run the comparison with the original spacing.
In Results select sense. Inspect the disturbance near the clock edge and read its peak.
Use the supplied 1.40 µm centerline spacing as the baseline. The high-impedance victim glitches when the nearby clock switches.
l-noise/space: Reduce the measured victim glitch below 85 mV by increasing clock spacing.
Open noise_space and choose Set clock spacing.
Increase the separation, then run the same clock comparison and read the peak on sense.
Set the clock centerline separation to 3.60 µm. Keep the stimulus and victim wiring fixed.
l-noise/layer: Compare the supplied metal2 clock with the same-layer baseline and state the model limit.
Open noise_layer and verify the clock path’s layer.
Run the comparison and read peak disturbance on sense with the same stimulus.
The included extractor reports zero coupling for this cross-layer case. The teaching model omits cross-layer coupling.
l-noise/shield: Record the shielded layout result and describe the modeled ground return.
Open noise_shield and trace the shield to its ground tie and far-end return.
Run the original clock stimulus and compare the peak and loading in Results.
Use the supplied shield with the ideal tie and 1 Ω return. The model includes shield loading. Electrostatic screening needs a field model.
l-supply/baseline: Measure the original supply drop under the fixed 1 mA load.
Open workspace and inspect the route length, width and endpoints.
Run the schematic/layout comparison. Read the difference between the source and load-side supply.
The 50 µm × 0.25 µm route gives 400 mV drop in the teaching interconnect model.
l-supply/repair: Reduce load-side supply drop to at most 150 mV with the same endpoints and load.
Select the long supply path, and adjust its Width in Properties.
Run the same comparison. Read the load supply and verify that the route still joins both endpoints.
Set the width to 0.80 µm. With the original 1 mA load the modeled drop becomes 125 mV.
l-floorplan/loose: Measure the initial macro footprint and distance from X1.OUT to X2.SOURCE.
Open workspace and locate the two placements and all five physical ports.
Find the metal1 obstacle and use Check this step to read area and pin-to-pin distance.
Use the original loose placement for this baseline. The exercise footprint exceeds 700 µm².
l-floorplan/compact: Fit both devices within 345 µm² and keep the signal pins within 12 µm before routing.
Choose Adjust macro placement. Move X2 closer while checking the obstacle remains in place.
Apply the new pitch and offset, then check footprint and pin distance. Leave the signal unrouted for the next lesson.
Set X2 pitch to 16 µm and row offset to 0 µm. Both device placements and ports remain intact.
l-access/access: Measure a legal metal1-only detour on the compact macro before adding any route.
Resume the compact macro from the floorplan lesson or compact it there first.
Open workspace and use Check this step to read the estimated metal1-only path around the obstruction.
Use 16 µm pitch and 0 offset. The metal1 detour is about 14.57 µm and slightly exceeds the short-route target.
l-access/route: Connect X1.OUT to X2.SOURCE within 14 µm and two vias, preserving the footprint and VSS.
Choose Plan pin route. Check that compact pitch and offset are still in place.
Permit a second metal layer if the metal1 detour is too long. Apply, then check length, via count and ports.
At 16 µm pitch and zero offset choose Metal1 and metal2. The 8.5 µm route uses two vias and retains the required ports.
l-pad-ring/trace: Find all incorrect or missing assignments in the starting pad map.
Open workspace and follow each perimeter route to its interior landing.
Use Check this step to record the unassigned and mismatched port names.
PWR and GND are unassigned. INA and INB are exchanged. Y already reaches its intended landing.
l-pad-ring/repair: Connect all five named ports to their correct perimeter pads.
Choose Assign perimeter pad and select a schematic port and landing. Apply each assignment separately.
Trace all five routes after assigning them and check the complete map.
PWR north, GND south, INA west upper, INB west lower and Y east. Keep the five underlying routes.
l-density/scan: Find the density window that fails and identify the sensitive line next to fill.
Open workspace and locate the two 20 × 20 µm measurement windows.
Use Check this step to record current metal1 coverage and inspect the right-side sensitive line.
The right window starts below 22%. The left window serves as the unchanged comparison.
l-density/close-fill: Capture a density-improving fill arrangement close enough to create a loading penalty.
Choose Configure window fill. Enter a small keepout and apply.
Use Check this step to measure coverage and estimated loading before trying a wider gap.
Use a 0.50 µm keepout for the close-fill reference. Density improves, but its loading exceeds the final limit.
l-density/repair: Meet 22–65% coverage with estimated added loading at or below 1.4 fF.
Reopen Configure window fill and increase the keepout from the sensitive net.
Regenerate fill and check both windows. Compare estimated capacitance with the close-fill reference.
Set a 2.50 µm keepout. The right window exceeds 22% and the modeled loading passes 1.4 fF.
l-antenna/fault: Identify the original conductor-to-gate area ratio at the early fabrication stage.
Open workspace and trace the metal1 conductor attached to the 1 µm² gate.
Use Check this step to read the connected metal area and compare the ratio with 12.
Keep the original long metal1 path for the baseline. Its area ratio exceeds the teaching limit of 12.
l-antenna/jumper: Meet the early-metal ratio of 12 while keeping the signal connected.
Open the jumper case and choose Add antenna repair.
Apply a layer transition and verify continuity and early-layer area in the checkpoint.
Choose Jump to metal2. The downstream segment remains connected while less early metal is attached to the gate at that stage.
l-antenna/diode: Meet the protected ratio of 32 using the exercise diode and the original early wire.
Open the diode case and choose Add antenna repair.
Attach the teaching diode and check the path and protected area ratio.
Choose Connect protection diode. Keep the long wire. The declared protected threshold is 32 in this lesson.
l-via-current/diagnose: Find the via current bottleneck with 1.2 mA total load and a 10 mV rail limit.
Open workspace and trace the supply current across the metal transition.
Use Check this step to read total drop and current per cut. Compare against both budgets.
The original total drop is below 10 mV, but each cut in the starting transition exceeds the 0.45 mA budget.
l-via-current/repair: Bring current per cut to at most 0.45 mA while preserving coverage and continuity.
Choose Configure via array. Estimate the number of cuts from 1.2/0.45 and select a viable rectangle.
Apply the array and check spacing/enclosure, supply connection and current per cut.
Use 2 rows × 2 columns. The equal-share current is 0.30 mA per cut.
l-isolation/ring: Close the guard’s active and metal paths and tie it only to quiet ground.
Open workspace, trace the existing guard perimeter and find the missing side.
Choose Add guard segment and restore that side. Check continuity to quiet and separation from the switching net.
Add the Top segment. The closed guard is verified on the quiet net.
l-isolation/taps: Attach enough covered guard contacts to leave no perimeter gap over 12 µm.
Choose Place guard contacts after closing the ring.
Increase the count and recheck cut coverage, quiet connectivity and maximum gap.
Choose 4 contacts. The largest verified gap is 11.4 µm.
l-spiral/reference: Capture the original spiral’s estimated inductance, resistance, Q and resonance.
Open spiral_reference. Trace the three-turn winding, underpass and matching contacts.
Use Check this step and write down the inductance, resistance, Q at 1 GHz and self-resonance.
Keep the supplied three-turn reference. Its values are the comparison for the candidate using the same lumped model.
l-spiral/candidate: Improve modeled Q at 1 GHz by over 5%, retain ≥1.8 nH and keep self-resonance above 3 GHz.
Open spiral_candidate and use Tune candidate coil.
Change one geometry field and check modeled Q, inductance and resonance against the reference.
Tune Turns to 4 with the original width and spacing. This candidate meets all three teaching limits.
l-handoff/fault: Identify the missing exported interface label while confirming geometry and hierarchy survive writing.
Resume the routed pass_macro project. Choose Export and inspect GDS.
Open Results and read the independently opened stream’s top cell, placed instances, layers and missing labels.
The actual stream has top pass_macro and two children, but lacks OUT. Judge the written bytes rather than the project sidecar.
l-handoff/verify: Export all expected pin-purpose labels with the same geometry and hierarchy.
Choose Assign stream pin label and pick the missing port on its original landing.
Export and inspect again. Check label layer and placement, the missing/extra lists and the reported checksum.
Assign OUT. Re-export with all five expected labels and unchanged mask geometry and hierarchy.
a-degeneration/baseline: Measure 10 kHz gain, THD and drain bias on the original common-source stage.
Choose Open workspace and trace RD, RS and the series VBIAS/VIN sources.
Run experiment, then Results. Record drain current and fundamental gain next to THD across harmonics 2–5.
The original bias is about 46.1 µA, gain 3.65 V/V and THD 5.98%.
a-degeneration/repair: Fit 43–49 µA bias, 1.25–2.8 V/V gain and ≤3% THD with the original load and sine.
Choose Edit source degeneration to increase RS and raise VBIAS enough to retain drain bias.
Run again and inspect Results. Compare THD only after verifying the bias and unchanged stimulus.
Use RS = 4k and VBIAS = .934 V. The measured result is about 46.0 µA, 1.64 V/V and 1.22% THD.
a-rejection/baseline: Record differential gain, CMRR and positive-rail PSRR for the original design at 10 kHz.
Run the three AC excitations and open Results. Read out at 10 kHz for the differential, common-mode and supply cases.
Use 20 log₁₀(Ad/Acm) and 20 log₁₀(Ad/As) with normalized positive magnitudes.
The original differential gain is about 1.12 V/V, CMRR −0.68 dB and input-referred PSRR+ 1.03 dB.
a-rejection/repair: Meet ≥28 dB CMRR, ≥30 dB PSRR+ and ≥1 V/V differential gain at 10 kHz.
Use Edit rejection circuit to raise tail resistance and add supply decoupling while preserving the bias and sources.
Run all three AC excitations. Compare the ratios only after checking Ad remains above 1 V/V.
Use RTAIL = 100k and CDEC = 1u. The result is about 30.2 dB CMRR, 33.6 dB PSRR+ and 1.27 V/V differential gain.
a-drive/baseline: Distinguish command error, own-final settling and bias current for 100 pF and 500 pF.
Open the source_follower reference. Run experiment for both loads.
In Results select command and out. Compare plateau error with the time to settle near the circuit’s own final voltage.
The follower misses the command by about 35.4 mV at both loads. Settling about its own final point slows from about 0.30 to 1.46 µs.
a-drive/repair: Meet 10 mV DC error, 4 µs settling and 35 mV peak overshoot on both feedback-buffer loads.
Open feedback_buffer and choose Edit compensation. Adjust CDOM while preserving the specified output stage.
Run experiment. In Results compare DC error, settling, overshoot and the original bias-current limit under both loads.
Use CDOM = 330p. DC error is about 6.22 mV, and settling is about 2.46 µs at 100 pF and 2.90 µs at 500 pF.
m-ramp/baseline: Locate the missing or nearly missing code in the 0–1 V ramp captures.
Choose Capture and measure ramp, then Results. Select Code density and display Code counts and DNL.
Compare adjacent comparator thresholds around the narrow bin. Confirm full code span and a monotonic input ramp.
Code 3 is missing in the supplied case. DNL there is −1 LSB because the neighboring thresholds nearly coincide.
m-ramp/repair: Recover all eight ramp codes with peak absolute DNL and INL no greater than 0.05 LSB.
Compare the resistors around the collapsed threshold bin and choose Edit ladder section.
Correct R4 while preserving the reference and ramp. Recapture and compare counts, transitions and both linearity plots.
Use R4 = 1k. The reference run gives 512 samples per code and zero sampled DNL and INL at the bench’s resolution.
project-chopper/baseline: Identify why the chopper fails to recover gain and compare ripple with the bypassed amplifier.
Open workspace and trace BMOD, BAMP, BDEMOD and the output filter.
Run experiment. Plot both 20 kHz clocks and compare recovered gain, offset and ripple across chopped and bypassed cases.
The starter VDEMOD delay is 12.5 µs, a quarter of the 50 µs period. It nearly cancels the recovered gain. Bypass offset is about 80 mV.
project-chopper/repair: Recover 19–21 V/V with <5 mV offset, ≤30 mV ripple and ≤700 µs average settling.
Use Edit demodulator and filter to align both clocks and tune CLP.
Run both cases. In Results verify the recovered gain, residual offset, ripple and settling together.
Use VDEMOD delay 0 and CLP = 10n. The measured gain is about 20 V/V, ripple 19 mV p-p and settling 350 µs.
project-relaxation/baseline: Measure nominal oscillator frequency, duty cycle and first rising edge.
Run the nominal experiment. In Results look at out, cap and trip around several crossings.
Use late cycles for period and duty. Read the first rising edge separately from the steady oscillation.
With original RT = 12k and CT = 10n, frequency is about 3.94 kHz, duty near 50%, and the first rise near 284 µs.
project-relaxation/corners: Fit 1.8–2.5 kHz, 46–54% duty, ≤850 µs startup and <15% frequency spread across corners.
Use Edit timing components. Increase the RC product to lower the frequency while retaining the Schmitt network.
Run all three conditions. Check frequency spread relative to nominal, duty and first edge in Results.
Use RT = 22k and CT = 10n. Frequencies are about 2174 Hz nominal, 2253 Hz cold/low rail and 2070 Hz hot/high rail.
project-pga/baseline: Identify the original programmable gain errors using AC and switching results for each code.
Choose Measure PGA response. Read each steady AC gain and −3 dB bandwidth.
Inspect gain-switching output plateaus and separate them from the AC measurements.
The starter gains are about 1.66, 2.99 and 5.96 V/V. The three states are below the 2×, 4× and 8× targets.
project-pga/repair: Meet the 2×, 4× and 8× gains within 3.5%, bandwidth ≥1 MHz and switching settling ≤12 µs.
Use 1 + RFB/RG as the starting equation and keep RFB and the switches fixed.
Choose Edit gain resistors. Run all gain states plus switching, then inspect low-frequency gain, bandwidth and settling.
Use RG1 = 20k, RG2 = 6.665k and RG3 = 2.856k. Measured gains are roughly 1.99, 3.98 and 7.92 V/V.
c-temperature/baseline: Capture the original ADC code span at 0 °C and 80 °C.
Open workspace and trace the shared reference and RTEMP/RFIX divider.
Choose Measure reference points. In Results read both ADC codes and subtract cold from hot.
Keep RFIX = 56k for this baseline. The original span is less than 55 counts over the anchors.
c-temperature/anchor: Get at least 55 counts of anchor span within codes 120–900 and calculate the calibration coefficients.
Use Edit sensor divider to shift the operating point and increase sensor-code span.
Measure both anchors again. Round 80,000 divided by span to the nearest integer, then multiply the cold code by the negative gain.
RFIX = 6.8k gives codes 588 and 646. Gain is 1379 m°C/count and offset is −810852 m°C.
c-temperature/validate: Meet ±0.8 °C at both anchors and ±2.5 °C across every held-out temperature and supply case.
Choose Edit calibration registers and enter the signed integer coefficients from the two anchors.
Run Validate held-out conditions and inspect the error plots at all three supplies, keeping validation separate from the anchor fit.
With RFIX = 6.8k, gain 1379 and offset −810852, all 15 held-out trials pass. Worst modeled error is about 2.23 °C.
inverter-process/build: Identify the selected process revision and bind the correct four-terminal inverter models.
Select the process in Student Hub, check its setup status and start the lesson.
Open workspace and inspect the linked PDK and each NMOS/PMOS model binding.
Use the two rated core models from the selected revision. Record the linked package, model names and supported analysis engine.
inverter-process/measure: Verify the selected process’s nominal inverter supply and record the revision.
Open the top testbench and select VDD. Read Value and compare it with the selected device class.
Record the actual process revision and nominal teaching operating point.
The provided supplies are 1.8 V for SKY130, 3.3 V for GF180 core and 1.2 V for IHP low-voltage devices.
inverter-schematic/build: Trace the inverter input, output, load, supply and four-terminal devices.
Open the testbench. Trace VIN to A, CL at Y and VDD through the supply port.
Choose Open inverter and read gate, drain, source and body labels in the child cell.
VIN drives A, CL loads Y, and the child receives power at VPWR and VGND.
inverter-schematic/measure: Verify the four-terminal CMOS inverter topology.
Open the inverter child. Select each transistor and read its terminal nets.
Trace each body with its source supply, then compare the joined input gates and output drains.
Both gates go to A and both drains to Y. NMOS source/body are VGND. PMOS source/body are VPWR.
inverter-dc/build: Capture the selected process’s DC transfer characteristic over its full supply range.
Verify the inverter wiring and configured ngspice runtime.
Choose Run lesson to sweep the input under the linked process models.
Use the provided DC sweep from 0 to the selected VDD with 200 intervals. Keep the process models and fixture fixed.
inverter-dc/measure: Verify DC endpoints and locate the switching threshold in the process-model sweep.
Open Results, plot VIN and VOUT and read high and low endpoints.
Find where VOUT crosses VIN and compare the threshold with the taught limits.
VOH must reach at least 90% VDD and VOL at most 10% VDD. VM is where VOUT = VIN and should fall at 20–80% VDD.
inverter-transient/build: Capture three transitions of the inverter under the normal 5 fF load.
Inspect the input pulse and load in the testbench.
Choose Run lesson and wait for the transient to finish under the linked process models.
Use the 20 ns input period, 5 fF load and supplied 62 ns run with requested 20 ps sample step.
inverter-transient/measure: Measure tPHL and tPLH using corresponding input/output 50% crossings.
Open Results to show both input and output. Mark their 50%-of-VDD thresholds.
Pair input rise with output fall and input fall with output rise. Confirm settled levels and three complete cycles.
Compute tPHL and tPLH from those crossing time differences. Use the measured load and process to report the delays.
inverter-layout/build: Create or open the inverter’s process layout for the selected cell.
Choose Build layout when the selected adapter supports native generation. For an imported cell, open its linked geometry.
Choose Open inverter in Layout and locate gates, diffusion, contacts and both supply rails.
The native generator builds one linked inverter layout for an empty cell. An imported geometry must correspond to the same process and schematic.
inverter-layout/measure: Verify all four physical ports and trace gate, output and supply conductors.
Open inverter in Layout. Select each physical port and view its corresponding terminal.
Follow the body/source return, shared gate and joined drains. Check the four assigned labels.
A is the input, Y the output, and VPWR/VGND the supplies with corresponding body ties. Verify all four physical ports.
inverter-drc/build: Capture an actual process-rule failure from a deliberate layout fault.
After building the supported layout, choose Add DRC fault. On imported geometry make a documented reversible width error.
Run lesson. Open Results and confirm the reported process rule and offending geometry before checking.
The native fault is an isolated undersized metal1 rectangle. An actual rule finding is the expected baseline evidence.
inverter-drc/measure: Repair the geometry fault and obtain a clean process DRC report.
Choose Repair lesson fault, or undo the documented manual geometry edit.
Run the same DRC again and verify the full report has zero violations.
Delete only the injected undersized rectangle. The scored result is a fresh process report with zero violations.
inverter-lvs/build: Capture an actual LVS mismatch with the layout intact.
Choose Add LVS fault for the supported layout, leaving physical geometry fixed.
Run the process verification. Open Results and identify the extracted device or parameter mismatch.
The native practice fault multiplies NMOS schematic width by 1.30. The extracted physical width remains original.
